messages:
maya: FYI — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I'm seeing KV memory growth and tail latency on longctx int8 sessions.
ops-bot: deploy completed by @derek 2026-03-17T22:10:00Z :white_check_mark:
derek: Yup. Canaries show p95 jump roughly 110ms -> 220ms for sessions >16k tokens (int8).
maya: Profiled GPU-7 process. KV resident pages ~1.9x, slab map has many small shards that aren't coalescing. flame snippet:
```
# kernel selection trace (condensed)
2026-03-17T22:11:02Z selector: choose kernel A (single-kernel)
2026-03-17T22:11:03Z remap: shard 0x7fa -> 0x8bc (memcpy 12MB)
2026-03-17T22:11:04Z selector: switch to kernel B (batched)
2026-03-17T22:11:04Z memcpy: 48MB
```
jin: Are we seeing more handoffs between shards or just more metadata objects? Could be selector oscillation.
anita: Dumped KV map. fragmentation metrics:
```
particle_count: 48000  # before: 12000
avg_shard_fill: 0.22   # before: 0.68
evict_ops/s: 38       # before: 9
```
samir: That aligns with the change to the grouping threshold — we reduced bucket size from 8->4, so small shard explosion expected.
derek: Right. The selector now favours 'single-kernel' for seq<128 to reduce warmup. But with long streaming it flips kernels on fragment boundaries, causing remaps and repeated GPU memcpy.
maya: Telemetry: KV page churn (page_in/page_out) +4x, memcpy bytes +83%, and int8 eval accuracy down ~0.6% on our regression set. BF16 shows no measurable accuracy drop but uses ~2.1x memory.
perf-bot: perf-summary: p50 34ms -> 40ms, p95 110ms -> 230ms, gpu_memcpy_bytes +83%, kv_pages_swapped +380%.
anita: Proposed mitigations: revert selector tweak for now; add hysteresis to shard handoff; cap kernel switches in a stream (eg once per 512 tokens).
samir: Plus consider merging small quantized shards proactively — int8 overhead for tiny shards kills both memory and perf. Maybe group by session_id % N to avoid pathological splits.
derek: I'll queue a rollback canary and a controlled probe that forces BF16 path on longctx to compare. @ops-bot can you schedule the canary?
ops-bot: canary rollback queued — id c-9876, expected completion in ~10m
maya: Thanks. I'm collecting per-request KV residency traces. If folks can add a histogram for shard handoffs and a memcpy hotspot flame that'll help pinpoint the hot loop.
jin: I'll add hist and a short flame. Also can we gate re-enabling the selector until we have a perf vs accuracy matrix for int8 vs bf16 vs fp16 on longctx?
maya: :thumbsup: Agreed. Let's reconvene after canary. Notes/PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234
